title: High-Performance Substrate — Security, Privacy & Doctrine Review

telemetry_redaction_implications.current_state: Content-light enforcement exists at application boundary (rig_relay/evidence/redaction.py) and event fabric boundary (rig_relay/events/store.py REDACT_FIELDS). 50 forbidden field keys. 5 pre-compiled regex patterns.

substrate_impact.zstandard_expansion: Zstandard compression must not obscure content-light inspection. All decompressed data must pass the same redaction scan as uncompressed data. Compression is storage optimization, not redaction bypass.
substrate_impact.parquet_snapshots: Parquet files are derived analytical snapshots. Content-light enforcement must apply during Parquet generation — no raw content fields may be projected into Parquet columns. CHECK equivalent: at generation time, verify no column name matches forbidden field patterns.
substrate_impact.arrow_batches: Arrow tables are in-memory transient. Content-light enforcement applies at table construction time — no forbidden fields in Arrow schema. Arrow is never persisted as a canonical artifact.
substrate_impact.postgres_copy: COPY FROM must use staging tables with CHECK constraints and INSERT triggers that enforce content-light. Never COPY directly to operational tables. Staging table rows that fail constraints are rejected with structured error — never silently dropped.
substrate_impact.pgvector_embeddings: Embeddings over private repo content are sensitive derived data. Must be local-only. Must never enter product telemetry. Must be classified as sensitive-derived-data in audit trail. Separate policy artifact required before pgvector implementation.
substrate_impact.pydantic_expansion: Pydantic model_validate with extra='forbid' provides type-level content-light enforcement. Fields not declared in the Pydantic model are rejected, preventing injection of forbidden fields through unknown keys.

compatible_tools: psycopg 3 COPY — strengthens Postgres as high-throughput operational substrate
pgvector — keeps vector search inside Postgres, avoiding database fragmentation
pg_jsonschema — defense-in-depth JSONB envelope validation at database boundary
incompatible_tools: LanceDB — fragments Postgres operational authority with separate vector database
Iceberg/Delta — replaces Postgres as operational substrate for analytics (wrong scale for local-first)
neutral_tools: Arrow/Parquet/Polars/DuckDB — read-side analytical tools that complement Postgres without replacing it
Ibis/DataFusion — query abstraction layers that can target Postgres as a backend

duckdb_implications.current_role: Disposable in-memory analytical microscope. Reads JSONL/Parquet files, produces projection data for cockpit widgets.
duckdb_implications.substrate_impact: DuckDB remains the primary analytical substrate for local mode. Postgres materialized views supplement DuckDB for operational dashboards in enterprise mode. Polars/Ibis/DataFusion are parked — DuckDB dominates the analytical need. If parked candidates are promoted, DuckDB must not be displaced — only supplemented.

json_jsonl_csv_source_of_truth_implicati.doctrine_reinforcement: All substrate tools must reinforce, not undermine, the artifact-first doctrine. No tool may produce output that is treated as canonical evidence without a corresponding JSON/JSONL/CSV artifact.

tool_specific_implications.parquet: Parquet snapshots MUST be classified as 'derived' in artifact_registry. They must be rebuildable from canonical JSONL. Parquet-never-canonical contract test required.
tool_specific_implications.arrow: Arrow tables are transient in-memory — never persisted. No Arrow files are canonical artifacts.
tool_specific_implications.zstandard: Zstandard-compressed bundles are storage optimization of canonical artifacts — the decompressed artifacts remain canonical. Bundle manifest records the SHA256 of the uncompressed canonical content.
tool_specific_implications.postgres_copy: Postgres tables are operational read replicas. COPY export back to JSONL must produce row count + SHA256 matches against canonical artifacts. Export manifest records equivalence.

cockpit_static_docs_procurement_implicat.cockpit: Postgres materialized views provide fresher widgets with lower latency. Arrow in-memory batches reduce dict-of-dicts overhead in projection payloads (if prototype succeeds). LISTEN/NOTIFY provides real-time projection invalidation (Postgres Phase 5). Cockpit must never display raw content — all widgets query content-light views only.
cockpit_static_docs_procurement_implicat.static_docs: Static docs renderer is a batch offline process. No substrate tool materially impacts rendering speed at current scale (~200 pages). At >1000 pages, Arrow batches could accelerate page generation. Parquet snapshots of schema registry could seed search index without re-reading all JSON files.
cockpit_static_docs_procurement_implicat.procurement: Zstandard-compressed evidence bundles reduce procurement pack size by 20-40%. Parquet rollups enable efficient historical query for procurement dashboards. psycopg COPY export provides fast procurement-grade evidence dumps. Procurement packs must be content-light by construction — no raw content in any exported artifact.

content_light_enforcement_continuity.doctrine: Every substrate tool must maintain or strengthen content-light enforcement. No tool may bypass the redaction boundary. No tool may introduce raw content into a stage that previously guaranteed content-light.
pipeline_enforcement_points: Stage 3 (Arrow): Arrow schema excludes forbidden field names
Stage 4 (Parquet): Parquet column names validated against forbidden patterns at generation time
Stage 5 (Postgres): CHECK constraints + INSERT triggers on all JSONB columns
Stage 6 (DuckDB): DuckDB queries select from content-light generated columns only
Stage 7 (cockpit/docs/packs): output scan for raw content before display/publish
